entries.name: The Clean Architecture
entries.why: The original article on the dependency rule between layers, which most mobile clean-architecture templates build on.

entries.name: Presentation Model
entries.why: The pattern MVVM grew out of: the view's state and behaviour kept in a class you can test without a UI.

entries.name: The Elm Architecture
entries.why: Model, update, view: the unidirectional loop behind TCA, Redux and BLoC, explained in a few short pages.

entries.name: Guide to app architecture (Android)
entries.why: Google's UI layer, data layer and unidirectional data flow guide; the same split is used on iOS, Flutter and React Native.

entries.name: Managing model data in your app
entries.why: Apple's walkthrough of `@Observable` models and who owns them with `@State`, `@Environment` and `@Bindable`.

entries.name: Migrating to the Observable macro
entries.why: The exact edits that move an `ObservableObject` view model to `@Observable`, and how view updates change.

entries.name: TN3187 UIKit scene-based life cycle
entries.why: Apple's technote for moving an app delegate-only app to `UIScene`, which apps built with the iOS 27 SDK must adopt.

entries.name: Swift 6 migration guide
entries.why: Data-race safety, `Sendable` and actor isolation step by step: the rules every Swift 6 architecture has to fit.

entries.name: Discover Observation in SwiftUI
entries.why: WWDC23 session on how Observation tracks the properties a view reads, the basis of current SwiftUI view models.

entries.name: The Composable Architecture
entries.why: Reducers, effects and dependencies in one library, with a test store that asserts every state change.

entries.name: Workflow (Swift)
entries.why: Square's composable state machines that render UI, with a matching Kotlin library for the Android app.

entries.name: Swift Sharing
entries.why: Shares and persists state between features (user defaults, files, memory) through one property wrapper.

entries.name: Swift Async Algorithms
entries.why: Debounce, throttle, merge and other `AsyncSequence` operators that replace Combine pipelines in view models.

entries.name: Swift Dependencies
entries.why: Environment-style dependency injection that also works outside views and swaps in test values per test.

entries.name: Factory
entries.why: Container-based injection with compile-time checked registrations and per-test overrides, without code generation.

entries.name: Needle
entries.why: Uber's compile-time checked dependency graph, generated from code and built for apps with many modules.

entries.name: Swinject
entries.why: Runtime container with object scopes, common in UIKit code bases that resolve dependencies at startup.

entries.name: Swift Navigation
entries.why: State-driven navigation for SwiftUI, UIKit and AppKit: a destination is an optional or an enum case in the model.

entries.name: XCoordinator
entries.why: Coordinator pattern for UIKit with typed routes, so view controllers no longer push each other.

entries.name: TCA example apps
entries.why: Case studies plus Todos, Voice Memos, SyncUps and Search apps, kept in step with each library release.

entries.name: Clean Architecture for SwiftUI
entries.why: SwiftUI app with SwiftData persistence, networking, dependency injection and unit tests in separate layers.

entries.name: iOS Clean Architecture MVVM
entries.why: UIKit template with a DI container, flow coordinators, DTO mapping and response caching across layers.

entries.name: SnapshotTesting
entries.why: Records views and values as reference files and fails on changes, catching UI regressions unit tests miss.

entries.name: Tuist
entries.why: Generates Xcode projects from Swift manifests, which keeps module boundaries explicit as an app grows.

entries.name: Guide to app architecture (Flutter)
entries.why: The Flutter team's recommended layers (UI, data, optional domain) built from views, view models and repositories.

entries.name: Architecture case study
entries.why: Walks through the Compass app to show the guide applied to real code, layer by layer.

entries.name: Architecture recommendations
entries.why: Each recommendation is rated strongly recommended, recommended or conditional, so you know what is optional.

entries.name: State management options
entries.why: The official index of state management approaches, with links to each package's own documentation.

entries.name: UIScene adoption
entries.why: What changes for the iOS runner of a Flutter app when `UIScene` becomes required, and how to migrate it.

entries.name: Bloc
entries.why: Events in, states out: business logic kept out of widgets and tested with `bloc_test`.

entries.name: Riverpod
entries.why: Compile-safe providers for async state, caching and dependency injection, testable without a widget tree.

entries.name: Provider
entries.why: A thin layer over `InheritedWidget` for injecting `ChangeNotifier` models; the Flutter docs start with it.

entries.name: MobX for Dart
entries.why: Observables, actions and reactions with code generation, for teams that prefer reactive state.

entries.name: Signals.dart
entries.why: Fine-grained reactive signals for Dart and Flutter that rebuild only the widgets reading a changed value.

entries.name: Freezed
entries.why: Generates immutable state classes, sealed unions and `copyWith`, removing boilerplate from state objects.

entries.name: get_it
entries.why: Service locator for repositories and services that is reachable outside the widget tree.

entries.name: go_router
entries.why: URL-based declarative routing maintained by the Flutter team, with deep links, redirects and nested navigators.

entries.name: Compass app
entries.why: The official sample behind the architecture guide, with unit, widget and integration tests.

entries.name: Flutter architecture samples
entries.why: One todo app built with BLoC, Redux, MobX, signals and more, so the approaches can be compared side by side.

entries.name: Bloc examples
entries.why: Counter, timer, login, todos, infinite list and weather apps, each built with bloc and covered by tests.

entries.name: Very Good CLI
entries.why: Creates apps and packages with a layered structure, tests and strict lints already set up.

entries.name: Melos
entries.why: Runs scripts, versioning and publishing across a Dart workspace when an app is split into feature packages.

entries.name: About the New Architecture
entries.why: Explains Fabric, TurboModules and JSI, the architecture new React Native apps have used by default since 0.76.

entries.name: Managing State (React)
entries.why: React's own guide to structuring state, lifting it up and moving it into reducers and context.

entries.name: Testing overview
entries.why: The official map of unit, component and end-to-end tests and which layer of an app each one covers.

entries.name: Redux Toolkit
entries.why: The official way to write Redux: slices, immutable updates written as mutations and RTK Query for server data.

entries.name: Zustand
entries.why: A small hook-based store that needs no provider; selectors keep re-renders limited to what changed.

entries.name: Jotai
entries.why: Atomic state: compose small atoms instead of one global store, with derived atoms for computed values.

entries.name: MobX
entries.why: Observable state with automatic dependency tracking; a component re-renders only when what it read changes.

entries.name: TanStack Query
entries.why: Keeps server data in its own layer with caching, refetching and retries, separate from UI state.

entries.name: XState
entries.why: State machines and statecharts for flows with many states and transitions, such as checkout or onboarding.

entries.name: Legend-State
entries.why: Fine-grained reactive state with built-in persistence, for apps that keep data on the device.

entries.name: Expo Router
entries.why: File-based routing for Expo and React Native apps, where every screen gets a URL and deep links work.

entries.name: React Navigation
entries.why: Stack, tab and drawer navigators for React Native; Expo Router is built on top of it.

entries.name: Ignite
entries.why: Infinite Red's boilerplate and generators: a complete app structure with state, navigation and tests.

entries.name: Obytes React Native template
entries.why: Expo and TypeScript starter with Expo Router, React Query, form handling and CI already wired together.

entries.name: React Native Testing Library
entries.why: Queries components the way a user finds them, so tests survive refactors of the code behind a screen.
